newsitem.title: CANADA: Doman CEO allowed to appeal punishment.
newsitem.headline: Doman CEO allowed to appeal punishment.

text.p: The British Columbia Court of Appeal said on Friday the chief executive of Doman Industries Ltd, a former British Columbia premier and his brother can appeal the punishment handed down in their insider trading conviction, a lawyer said.

Marvin Storrow, who represents Doman chief executive Herb Doman, said the court had previously granted the trio leave to appeal the underlying conviction on insider trading. The full appeal will look at both that finding of guilt and the penalty.
A date for the proceeding has not yet been set.

The three were barred from trading securities and serving as officers or directors of a public company for 10 years. The court previously ruled that Doman could remain in his post while the case was appealed.
The British Columbia Securities Commission in August announced that Doman, former British Columbia premier Bill Bennett and his brother Russell Bennett were found guilty of insider trading.
Storrow said the court ruled they could appeal their punishment because they were not given a chance to present arguments against the penalty.
The insider-trading case lasted eight years and revolved around the collapse in 1988 of a takeover bid by Louisiana-Pacific Corp for Doman.

Doman was accused of passing along a tip to Russell Bennett that the takeover had fallen through. The Bennetts sold all their Doman shares minutes before trading was halted for the announcement of the news. Regulators said the Bennetts made a C$2 million profit.

Doman and the Bennetts vehemently denied the allegations. They were acquitted of similar charges in 1989. Regulators pursued the case through legal battles that went all the way to the Supreme Court of Canada.
